explanation: The claw snaps shut so fast that it fires a jet of water. A bubble forms and collapses with a loud crack, and colonies of these shrimps make the reef crackle.

claims.text: Pistol (snapping) shrimp stun prey by snapping a specialized claw, which creates a collapsing bubble and a shock wave.
Fiddler crabs, hermit crabs and coconut crabs do not stun prey with shock waves from their claws.
The pistol shrimp's snap fires a fast jet of water that forms a cavitation bubble, which collapses with a loud crack.
Colonies of snapping shrimp produce a constant crackling sound on reefs.

evidence.restatement: Pistol shrimp snap an enlarged claw, creating a collapsing cavitation bubble whose shock wave stuns prey.
Fiddler, hermit and coconut crabs do not stun prey with shock waves from their claws.
The snap fires a fast water jet; the cavitation bubble it forms collapses with a loud crack (Versluis and colleagues, 2000).
Colonies of snapping shrimp make the constant crackle heard on reefs.
